154703723.title: File:Saint Sergius and Saint Bacchus, from Saint Catherine Monastery, Mount Sinai, second half of the 13th century.jpg

ObjectName.value: Saint Sergius and Saint Bacchus, from Saint Catherine Monastery, Mount Sinai, second half of the 13th century

Categories.value: Pages with non-numeric formatnum arguments|PD-old-100-expired|PD-Art (PD-old-100-expired)|13th-century icons|CC-PD-Mark|Icons from Saint Catherine Monastery, Mount Sinai|Icons of Georgia (country)|PD-Art missing SDC copyright status|PD-old missing SDC copyright status|Kingdom of Eastern Georgia|Icons of Serge and Bacchus

ImageDescription.value:
Georgian warriors icon from Saint Catherine Monastery, Mount Sinai, second half of the 13th century.

"Beginning with the second third of the thirteenth century, the military equipment and combat style of the Georgians changed under the inluence of the Mongols: the bow was added to the obligatory military equipment. Despite this, the lance remained the basic weapon, losing its old signiicance only in the latter half of the eighteenth century. Note 68: Mamuka Tsurtsumia, “Sinas mtis tsminda mkhedrebi” [Warrior Saints of Mount Sinai], Kartvelologia 12 (2008), 13–44, p. 32) in (1 January 2014). "Couched Lance and Mounted Shock Combat in the East: The Georgian Experience". Journal of Medieval Military History, vol. XII: 93."

Also: (1 January 2020). "კვლავ ერთიანი მონარქიის დროშის შესახებ. Once More about the Standard of Unified Georgia". Heraldy, ჰეროლდი 9: 110.

Also: Depiction of Saint Sergius and Saint Bacchus.(2005) Crusader Art in the Holy Land, From the Third Crusade to the Fall of Acre, 1187-1291, p. 337ff
